analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: TransitionWatchdogTests.swift (new), AutopilotTinyModelTests.swift (new), and an added assertion in ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (lines 683-687). No production code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, or encryption path is modified, so no new attack surface or weakened control is introduced by this diff.

Security-relevant behavior the tests exercise, which the next pass should check against production sources not supplied here: (1) the transition watchdog (stall bounds of 600s/300s) cancels only the autopilot operation and the startup-preload driver, answers a stalled legacy preload with 'transition_stalled' without interrupting another owner's load, and does nothing without consent (TransitionWatchdogTests lines 271-285). (2) Autopilot adoption and hold semantics: an inventory model adopted under an operation-scoped lease keeps serving after the lease ends until an admin unload, and requires a verified weight hash (AutopilotTinyModelTests line 261). That is relevant to T-027 and T-012 weight-substitution assumptions. It also touches the consent and lease boundary, but production enforcement is unverified from these tests alone. (3) The model-switch test asserts that .modelSwitch is released on failure while .draining and refusingNewWork remain set only on an unconfirmed commit. That is consistent with fail-closed admission behavior. (4) The downloaded-build test relies on the publication step verifying cached bytes before the model joins the selected set.

The tests use attestationSigner nil, scripted memory and download stubs, and test-only hooks on ProviderLoop (for example installStartupDriverForTesting). Whether those hooks are compiled only into test targets is unverified, but they are declared in a test-file private extension, so they are not production surface. The production watchdog and autopilot implementation is not in this batch, so I make no conclusion on its correctness.
